note:
Class 6B, week of 16 November. Notes for myself.

Aarav Sharma has missed four days this month. His mother Sunita told me on the phone (98765 43210) that his father lost his job at the mill and the family cannot pay for anything extra this term; Aarav now helps at the family tea stall before school. He is bright in maths but has not handed in homework for two weeks.

Meenal reads well aloud but freezes in written tests. She needs extra writing practice, and the remedial writing club meets after the last bell. She told me she has epilepsy and is afraid of having a seizure in the exam hall. Her roll no. 6B/23. She walks six kilometres home to Rampur Kalan and has to leave school at the last bell to reach home before dark.

Kabir and Ishaan fight most days during group work. Kabir's parents are separating and he is staying with his grandmother. Ishaan finishes early and gets bored.

Tanvi is far ahead in reading. She could help others, but she is shy. Her family does not have a smartphone or an internet connection. Every Tuesday she goes with her grandmother to the town clinic and has to miss school that day, and her mother cooks in two homes until evening.

Lesson
Class: Class 6
Subject: English
Topic: Writing a short description of a place
Length: 40 minutes

draft.title: Class 6 English — Writing a Short Description of a Place

items.heading: Starter (5 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: Close your eyes and think of your favorite room at home or a quiet park you know well. Write on the chalkboard the heading: Places We Know. Ask the pupils to open their notebooks and write down three words that describe the sights, sounds, or smells of that place using only their pens.

items.heading: Teach (10 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: A good description helps the reader see, hear, and feel the place through simple details. Write the following model paragraph on the chalkboard: My small classroom has bright yellow walls and a large wooden desk at the front. Through the open window, I can hear the cheerful chirping of birds in the tall neem tree. When the afternoon breeze blows inside, it carries the earthy scent of damp soil after rain. Ask the pupils to copy this model into their notebooks using their pens.

items.heading: Practise (15 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: Now write your own short description of a place you like using the model on the chalkboard as a guide. Write on the chalkboard: Include three sentences about what you see, hear, and smell. Ask the pupils to open their notebooks and write their descriptions independently using their pens.

items.heading: Check (10 minutes)
items.text: Say to the class: Exchange notebooks with your partner and read their description quietly. Write on the chalkboard: Check if your partner included one detail for sight, one for sound, and one for smell. Ask the pupils to return the notebooks and tell their partners one thing they liked about the written description.

items.heading: Homework
items.text: Say to the class: For homework, you will write one final paragraph describing your kitchen or the path you take walking to school. Write on the chalkboard: Homework: Write four descriptive sentences in your notebook about your kitchen or your walk to school. Ask the pupils to copy this task into their notebooks using their pens.
